dimensions.assessment: Involves multiple federal agencies, state, local, and tribal governments, broadband providers, and individuals in the United States lacking high-speed internet.
dimensions.evidence: providing high-speed, affordable broadband internet access service to all individuals in the United States

dimensions.assessment: Requires strategic planning, interagency coordination, reporting, and administrative streamlining rather than direct funding changes.
dimensions.evidence: develop and implement a national strategy to improve the coordination and management of federal broadband programs

dimensions.assessment: Requires the strategy to address the cost and sources of resources needed, but does not appropriate specific funding amounts.
dimensions.evidence: address the cost of the Strategy, the sources and types of resources and investments needed

dimensions.assessment: Involves coordination across 14 distinct federal agencies and programs, plus state, local, and tribal entities.
dimensions.evidence: The term covered agencies means... [lists 14 agencies]

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing reporting requirements, regular briefings, and periodic reviews over a multi-year framework.
dimensions.evidence: not less frequently than once every 90 days thereafter until the date on which the Implementation Plan is fully implemented

missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for strategy execution
Specific number of state and local entities that will participate
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the NTIA to develop a national strategy and implementation plan to improve coordination of federal broadband programs, reduce barriers for state, local, and tribal governments, and report periodically to Congress.
